sources.title: Is the Sun causing global warming?
sources.note: No upward satellite-era incoming-solar-energy trend; not a stand-alone test of every indirect solar mechanism.

sources.title: A history of solar activity over millennia
sources.locator: Section 4.1, Millennial Eddy cycle and Hallstatt cycle; proxy discussion
sources.note: Eddy not significant in assessed reconstruction; Hallstatt evidence qualified by limited record length.

sources.title: Holocene solar activity inferred from global and hemispherical cosmic-ray proxy records
sources.locator: Abstract, Main and Methods, including radionuclide data and Bayesian model
sources.note: Attributes millennial radionuclide variability to geomagnetic changes. Hemispheric archive and model assumptions remain important.

sources.authors: Maximilian Arthus Schanner, Andreas Nilsson and Raimund Muscheler
sources.title: Joint Inversion of Radionuclide Production Rate Data and Thermoremanent Magnetic Records over the Holocene
sources.note: Joint inversion does not require explicit long-term solar component; shares authors and methodological lineage with S03.

sources.title: 9,400 years of cosmic radiation and solar activity from ice cores and tree rings
sources.locator: Results, discussion of periodicities, conclusions and computational analysis
sources.note: Reports significant Eddy-scale periodicity and regional climate association; does not establish solar-only modern attribution.

sources.authors: I. G. Usoskin, Y. Gallet, F. Lopes, G. A. Kovaltsov and G. Hulot
sources.title: Solar activity during the Holocene: the Hallstatt cycle and its consequence for grand minima and maxima
sources.locator: Author manuscript abstract; journal reference Astronomy & Astrophysics 587, A150
sources.note: Shared approximately 2400-year secondary SSA component interpreted as solar; full numerical method replication pending.

sources.authors: I. G. Usoskin, S. K. Solanki and G. A. Kovaltsov
sources.title: Grand minima and maxima of solar activity: New observational constraints
sources.note: Early stochastic/chaotic interpretation; must not be quoted as the final word while ignoring later S06.

sources.title: Persistent solar influence on North Atlantic climate during the Holocene
sources.locator: Original article abstract and bibliographic record
sources.note: North Atlantic proxy correlations and proposed amplification; not a measured global temperature or modern attribution series.

sources.title: IntCal13 and Marine13 Radiocarbon Age Calibration Curves 0–50,000 Years cal BP
sources.note: Radiocarbon calibration, not a direct solar-forcing or temperature product.

sources.title: Solar influences on climate
sources.note: Includes UV, ozone and dynamical pathways. Existence of a pathway is distinct from its global attribution magnitude.

sources.title: Correction to Solar influences on climate
sources.note: Use corrected figures if reproducing S10; no figures from that review are reproduced in Stage A.

sources.title: No evidence for globally coherent warm and cold periods over the preindustrial Common Era
sources.note: Preindustrial epoch timing differs by region. Authors recommend a companion global-mean reconstruction for global-mean analyses.

sources.title: Climate of the Past, Present and Future: A Scientific Debate, 2nd edition
sources.locator: Book metadata/abstract; user-supplied figures; full-book audit pending
sources.note: Critical Science Press. Reference and hypothesis source; no claim of having read or validated every chapter.

sources.title: The Winter Gatekeeper Hypothesis (VII). A summary plus Q&A
sources.note: Acknowledges anthropogenic warming; reduced human share is conditional. Primary evidence of author position, not validation of the hypothesis.

sources.title: AR6 Chapter 7: The Earth's Energy Budget, Climate Feedbacks, and Climate Sensitivity
sources.note: Explicitly assesses solar forcing. Preserve cycle-averaged versus single-year and likely versus very-likely conventions.

sources.title: Solar cycles or random processes? Evaluating solar variability in Holocene climate records
sources.locator: Abstract, introduction and random-walk test description; linked corrigendum requires separate review before reproducing results
sources.note: Methodological warning about stochastic periodicities, not proof that all solar cycles are spurious.

sources.authors: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies
sources.title: GISS Surface Temperature Analysis, GISTEMP v4, data product landing page
sources.locator: Data product landing page checked 2026-09-05; year is access year, not release date
sources.note: Instrument-based temperature analysis; actual versioned source files have not been acquired in this project.

sources.authors: NOAA NCEI; Odele Coddington, Judith Lean and Peter Pilewskie
sources.title: NOAA Climate Data Record of NASA NOAA LASP Total Solar Irradiance, NNLTSI Version 3
sources.locator: Product and metadata pages checked 2026-09-05; year is access year, not release date
sources.note: Model-derived irradiance CDR constrained by observations, not direct satellite measurements throughout its historical extent.

sources.title: Solar and Anthropogenic Climate Drivers: An Updated Regression Model and Refined Forecast
sources.locator: Publisher metadata and author preprint abstract; full-method review pending
sources.note: Retained as a recent competing interpretation, not treated as validated attribution; endpoint and coefficient choices require audit.
